newsitem.title: USA: Mississippi court allows tobacco suit to proceed.
newsitem.headline: Mississippi court allows tobacco suit to proceed.

text.p: The Mississippi Supreme Court on Thursday rejected Gov. Kirk Fordice's legal challenge to a landmark tobacco lawsuit brought by his own attorney general, a spokesman for the attorney general said.
"It looks like they ruled for us," said Special Assistant Attorney General Trey Bobinger, a spokesman for Mississippi Attorney General Mike Moore.
Bobinger provided no details but said a news conference had been scheduled for 1430 CST/2030 GMT.

Fordice, a Republican, had challenged the lawsuit brought by Moore, a Democrat. The suit seeks compensation from tobacco companies for state Medicaid funds spent treating poor people for smoking-related illnesses.
The governor contended that only he had the authority to bring lawsuits to recover Medicaid money since Mississippi's division of Medicaid is under the control of his office.
If the court had ruled in Fordice's favor, Moore's lawsuit would have been limited to claims on behalf of charity hospital spending and the prohibition of cigarette advertising aimed at children.
